articles.title: CFMoto 550MT and 550MT-X Unveiled at EICMA 2026
articles.categoryDescription: Recent news and new launches: vehicles, gadgets, AI and aviation, explained from official sources.
articles.excerpt: CFMoto showed two new middleweight adventure motorcycles in Milan on 4 November 2026, both with a new 526 cc twin making 54 hp. Prices and dates are not yet announced.
blocks: CFMoto unveiled two new adventure motorcycles, the **550MT** and the **550MT-X**, at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan. The company's UK page is dated 4 November 2026. Both bikes use a new 526 cc parallel-twin engine that makes 40 kW (54 hp) at 8,500 rpm and 52 Nm of torque at 6,000 rpm. CFMoto has not announced prices or on-sale dates, and this article is written as of 6 November 2026.

According to CFMoto's UK page, the 550MT is the touring-focused model and the 550MT-X is the off-road-focused one. The company says the figures shown are development-phase data and may change for production. UK prices and arrival dates are listed as "to be confirmed". CFMoto has not published an India price or an India launch plan in the sources checked for this article.
CFMoto's Benelux news page says the company held two press conferences on the show's press day and that the Global Brand Ambassador Mario Román joined the unveiling of the 550MT-X on stage.

Engine: new 526 cc liquid-cooled parallel twin, 40 kW (54 hp) at 8,500 rpm, 52 Nm at 6,000 rpm
Fully adjustable KYB suspension at both ends
Bi-directional quickshifter (works for upshifts and downshifts)
A six-speed gearbox, according to the Malaysian outlet paultan.org

The 550MT has a 23-litre fuel tank, cruise control and an 800 mm seat that adjusts up to 820 mm. It runs a 19-inch front and a 17-inch rear wheel, according to paultan.org. CFMoto lists an inertial measurement unit (IMU), a sensor that tracks the bike's lean and movement, which supports Bosch cornering ABS and traction control. It also has a rear detection system (RDS) for traffic behind the rider.

The cockpit has an 8-inch MMI 2.0 display with Apple CarPlay, and a smart key that works through Bluetooth and NFC. An electronic-clutch version is listed as optional, which means the rider does not need to use the clutch lever for pulling away and stopping.

The 550MT-X has 230 mm of front and 220 mm of rear suspension travel and 250 mm of ground clearance. Its wheels are 21 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear, with CST tyres, J.Juan brakes and discs of 320 mm at the front and 240 mm at the rear. It has a 16-litre tank and an 850 mm seat that adjusts down to 830 mm.

CFMoto gives a dry weight of 172 kg, which it says is 3 kg less than the 450MT, with around 30 per cent more power. The X has a ride-by-wire throttle, three riding modes, switchable ABS and traction control, and a vertical 6.2-inch display with Motoplay connectivity.

Fuel tank: 550MT 23 litres; 550MT-X 16 litres
Seat height: 550MT 800 mm (adjustable to 820 mm); 550MT-X 850 mm (adjustable to 830 mm)
Dry weight: 550MT not yet listed; 550MT-X 172 kg
Display: 550MT 8-inch with CarPlay; 550MT-X 6.2-inch vertical
ABS and traction control: 550MT IMU-based; 550MT-X switchable
Where it sits in the range

Paultan.org describes the 550MT as positioned above the 450MT, whose Malaysian price it gives as RM28,888, and notes that CFMoto's current adventure line also includes the 700MT and 800MT Explore. The Benelux page adds that CFMoto showed a future platform idea built on the same 550 engine, with a lightweight aluminium frame and a configurable electronic clutch, but this was a vision and not a product announcement.

A **parallel twin** has two cylinders side by side. A **quickshifter** lets the rider change gear without using the clutch lever or closing the throttle. **Dry weight** is the weight without fuel, oil and other fluids, so the weight on the road is higher. **Cornering ABS** adjusts the anti-lock brake limit for the bike's lean angle, using the IMU readings.
Seat height and ground clearance are manufacturer figures measured under set conditions, and CFMoto notes that the development motorcycles in its photographs may carry accessories.

Price in any market, including India
On-sale dates
Final production specifications
Dry weight of the 550MT
Everything above is the manufacturer's published information from the show. Production bikes may differ, and no ride impressions exist yet.

articles.title: KTM 450 RC Sportbike Shown at EICMA 2026 (Nov 2026)
articles.categoryDescription: Recent news and new launches: vehicles, gadgets, AI and aviation, explained from official sources.
articles.excerpt: KTM surprised the EICMA show with the 2028 KTM 450 RC, a twin-cylinder supersport bike. Production is planned for late 2027, and full specifications are still to come.
blocks: KTM showed the **2028 KTM 450 RC**, a new twin-cylinder supersport motorcycle, at EICMA in Milan in early November 2026. KTM's press release calls it an "unexpected appearance". Production is planned for late 2027, and the bike will arrive as a model-year 2028 motorcycle. KTM says full technical specifications and market availability will be announced closer to the start of production. This article is written as of 6 November 2026.
What KTM says about the bike

KTM describes the 450 RC as a KTM-engineered motorcycle with its own chassis setup, calibration and specifications, aimed at the entry and mid-displacement sportbike segment. The release does not give an engine output, weight or price.

Front suspension: 43 mm WP APEX upside-down fork, adjustable for compression and rebound
Rear suspension: WP APEX shock on a single-sided swingarm, adjustable for preload and rebound
Front brake: single 320 mm disc with a four-piston radial WP caliper
Tyres: Pirelli Diablo Rosso 4 as standard
Electronics: cornering ABS, MTC dual-channel ABS with Road and Supermoto modes, and multiple ride modes
Display and ports: 5-inch TFT dashboard, USB-A and USB-C charging
KTM says the single-disc front brake reduces unsprung weight, which is the weight of parts that are not carried by the suspension.

Several outlets add details that are not in KTM's press release, so treat them as reports and not as KTM's own figures. BikeWale says the bike is based largely on the CFMoto 450SR-S, shares its frame and engine with it, and quotes 56 bhp and 48 Nm, adding that it expects a restriction to 48 bhp for Europe's A2 licence. SpeedWeek reports that the frame, engine and swingarm are identical to the CFMoto model, and that the 450 RC was unveiled for the Chinese market in April 2026. BikeWale also reports that the bike is not planned for India and will go on sale in Europe in 2028.
KTM's own release, as read for this article, does not name CFMoto or state the engine details. The company has not published a price.
Why it matters to Indian readers

BikeWale reports that KTM is not planning the 450 RC for India and points to a separate parallel-twin platform it has seen testing in Europe. KTM has not confirmed that in the release read here, so the India position is an outlet report only.

A **supersport** motorcycle is a road bike built around track-style handling and a forward-leaning riding position. **Cornering ABS** adjusts the brake limit for the lean angle. **MTC** is KTM's motorcycle traction control; the dual-channel ABS system works on both wheels, and the Supermoto mode, per KTM, is one of the settings on the brake system. The A2 licence mentioned by BikeWale is a European licence class that limits a rider's first bike to 35 kW (about 47.5 hp), so makers often offer bikes in that class.

KTM has deliberately left out power, torque and weight, so any number seen elsewhere is not a KTM figure at this stage. The suspension, brake and electronics details above are the ones KTM itself lists. A reader comparing it with other small sportbikes should wait for the full specification, because the figures that decide a comparison, such as weight and output, are exactly the ones still missing.

April 2026: SpeedWeek says the 450 RC was unveiled for the Chinese market
Early November 2026: KTM shows the bike at EICMA, Milan
Late 2027: KTM's planned start of production
Model year 2028: arrival as a 2028 motorcycle, per KTM

Official power, torque and weight figures for the European bike
Price in any market
On-sale date by market
Which markets besides Europe will get it
The year in the name is the model year: the 2028 KTM 450 RC is planned to enter production in late 2027.

articles.title: CFMoto V4SR-RR Superbike Shown at EICMA 2026
articles.categoryDescription: Recent news and new launches: vehicles, gadgets, AI and aviation, explained from official sources.
articles.excerpt: CFMoto showed its V4SR-RR superbike at EICMA 2026: a 997 cc V4, active aerodynamic winglets and about 180 kg dry weight. No price or sales date has been announced.
blocks: CFMoto presented its **V4SR-RR** superbike at the EICMA motorcycle show in Milan in November 2026. CFMoto's Benelux news page describes a 997 cc, 90-degree V4 engine with more than 210 horsepower, a 15,000 rpm limit and a top speed of over 315 km/h, plus active aerodynamics with independently controlled winglets. CFMoto has not announced a price or a sales date. This article is written as of 6 November 2026.

CFMoto says the V4SR-RR was first unveiled at EICMA 2024. BikeWale reports that the bike has been seen testing on track and on display several times before, and that the show reveal is the official presentation of the production-looking model.

Engine: in-house 997 cc, 90-degree V4, over 210 pk (horsepower) according to CFMoto
Rev limit: up to 15,000 rpm
Top speed: over 315 km/h, according to CFMoto
Dry weight: approximately 180 kg (without fluids)
Suspension: fully adjustable Öhlins
Brakes: Brembo Hypure Sport
Tyres: Pirelli Diablo Supercorsa SP V4
Exhaust: full titanium Akrapovič system

CFMoto says the bike has an active aerodynamic system with independently controllable winglets, shaped by the rule "form follows performance". BikeWale describes the front surfaces as able to move up and down, giving up to 20 per cent more downforce at higher speeds, or to fold flat to lower drag. Downforce here means air pressure pushing the bike toward the ground. The 20 per cent figure comes from BikeWale, not from the CFMoto page read for this article.

CFMoto lists a patented, adjustable frame reinforcement system that works with the Öhlins suspension. BikeWale adds that the chassis geometry can be adjusted by the owner and that the frame is a front-frame design.

CFMoto also showed the V4SR-RR Carbon Black, which it calls an exclusive show bike. It has extensive carbon-fibre bodywork, an Akrapovič exhaust, GILLES Tooling parts and an STM dry anti-hop clutch derived from MotoGP technology. BikeWale reports that the Akrapovič exhaust is optional on the standard bike and that, with it, output rises to 218 bhp; it also gives 215 bhp in its headline, so power figures differ between sources.

The numbers above are what the makers and outlets state, and they were produced for a show launch, not a test. Top speed and weight are claims, and the active aero gain is described by an outlet in per cent terms without a stated test method. A buyer comparing it with other litre-class superbikes should wait for homologated specifications, which are the figures regulators and dealers will publish with the price.

Power: CFMoto says over 210 pk; BikeWale's text says 210 bhp, 218 bhp with the optional exhaust, and its headline says 215 bhp
Top speed: both sources say 315 km/h, which CFMoto presents as over 315 km/h

A **V4** engine has four cylinders arranged in two banks of two; here the banks are set at 90 degrees. **Winglets** are small wing-shaped surfaces on the fairing. **Dry weight** excludes fuel, oil and coolant. An **anti-hop clutch** limits rear-wheel hopping when the rider downshifts hard. **Front-frame** designs use a frame that connects the steering head to the engine instead of a full perimeter around it.

CFMoto's Benelux page also reports group turnover of more than 3.11 billion US dollars in the first three quarters of 2026, up 40.59 per cent on the same period a year earlier, and R&D spending of 186 million US dollars. Those are company figures and are not audited in the source.

Price in any market, including India
A sales date
Homologation details for road use in each region
These are manufacturer claims from a show presentation. No independent test figures have been published.
